key_insight: Epitaxial α-MnTe thin films on InP(111) show transport signatures consistent with a finite net magnetic polarization, despite bulk MnTe being compensated antiferromagnetic.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a thin-film engineering route to tune magnetic response in MnTe for spintronic device concepts.
method: Molecular beam epitaxy growth of epitaxial α-MnTe on InP(111).
Low-temperature magneto-transport measurements of longitudinal and transverse responses.
DFT calculations to test bulk, interface, and defect-driven origins of magnetization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a hysteretic butterfly longitudinal magnetoresistance and a nonlinear transverse magnetoresistance, together with DFT results supporting symmetry breaking and defect-driven magnetization pathways.
watch_item: Transport signatures indicate magnetic polarization, but the mechanism may depend sensitively on interface quality, strain, and point defects rather than being intrinsic to ideal bulk MnTe.
paper_title: Transport Evidence of Magnetic Polarization in the Altermagnetic Candidate MnTe
